setName: Day 6 · Major Stanza Forms: Sonnet, Ballad, Elegy, Ode, Epic & Mock Epic

questions.question: In poetry, what is a stanza?
options: The repeated sound at a word ending
A group of lines arranged as a unit within a poem
A prose paragraph in a novel
A pause inside a single metrical line
questions.explanation: A stanza groups verse lines into a unit, often separated visually from other groups.

questions.question: A stanza made up of four lines is called a:
questions.explanation: A quatrain has four lines regardless of whether its lines rhyme.

questions.question: Which rhyme scheme characterizes a traditional ottava rima stanza?
questions.explanation: Ottava rima has eight lines and normally rhymes ABABABCC.

questions.question: A seven-line stanza in iambic pentameter rhymes ABABBCC. What is its name?
questions.explanation: The seven-line ABABBCC pattern identifies rhyme royal, associated with Chaucer.

questions.question: Which feature distinguishes a Spenserian stanza from an ordinary set of nine pentameter lines?
options: Its first line must be a rhyming couplet
Its ninth line is an alexandrine, typically iambic hexameter
Its ninth line has no metre
It consists of three equal tercets
questions.explanation: The Spenserian stanza has eight pentameter lines followed by a longer, six-foot alexandrine.

questions.question: If linked tercets begin ABA BCB, which rhyme pattern would normally follow in terza rima?
questions.explanation: The middle rhyme of a tercet becomes the outer rhyme of the following one: ABA BCB CDC.

questions.question: Two stanza patterns are ABABBCC and ABABABCC. Which pairing identifies them correctly?
questions.explanation: ABABBCC belongs to seven-line rhyme royal; ABABABCC belongs to eight-line ottava rima.

questions.question: A student claims that a Spenserian stanza and a Spenserian sonnet have the same length. Which correction is accurate?
options: The stanza has nine lines; the sonnet has fourteen
Both have fourteen lines and identical rhyme patterns
Both have eight lines but different metres
The stanza has fourteen lines; the sonnet has nine
questions.explanation: A Spenserian stanza has nine lines, whereas the Spenserian sonnet follows a fourteen-line pattern.

questions.question: How many lines does a traditional sonnet contain?
questions.explanation: The traditional sonnet is a lyric form of fourteen lines.

questions.question: What is the usual structural division of a Shakespearean sonnet?
options: Three quatrains followed by a couplet
An octave followed by a sestet
Four tercets followed by a refrain
questions.explanation: The Shakespearean sonnet comprises twelve lines arranged in three quatrains plus a final couplet.

questions.question: In what order do the two principal sections appear in a conventional Petrarchan sonnet?
questions.explanation: An Italian or Petrarchan sonnet conventionally divides into eight lines and six lines.

questions.question: Which pattern is most characteristic of the opening octave of a Petrarchan sonnet?
questions.explanation: The Petrarchan octave typically uses enclosed rhymes in the pattern ABBAABBA.

questions.question: Which full rhyme scheme identifies the standard Shakespearean sonnet?
questions.explanation: The standard English sonnet uses three independently rhymed quatrains and a final GG couplet.

questions.question: What does the term "volta" mean in sonnet analysis?
options: A fixed pause after every fourth syllable
The repeated opening word of each stanza
The final stressed syllable of a line
A turn or shift in thought or argument
questions.explanation: The volta marks a change in the poem’s direction of thought, often near a structural boundary.

questions.question: A sonnet uses ABAB BCBC CDCD EE. Which subtype best fits this rhyme scheme?
questions.explanation: The linked B and C rhymes across quatrains distinguish the Spenserian sonnet.

questions.question: A fourteen-line poem rhymes ABBAABBA CDECDE, and its argument turns after line eight. Which reading is most precise?
options: It is a rhyme-royal stanza followed by a sestet
It is a Shakespearean sonnet with three independent quatrains
It is ottava rima followed by a heroic quatrain
It is a Petrarchan sonnet with the volta at the octave-sestet boundary
questions.explanation: The enclosed octave and six-line response form a conventional Petrarchan sonnet.

questions.question: A fourteen-line poem has three independently rhymed quatrains and ends with a couplet that overturns the earlier claim. What most strongly identifies its form?
options: The structural build-up and final couplet of a Shakespearean sonnet
The seven-line grouping of rhyme royal
The eight-plus-six division of a Petrarchan sonnet
The interwoven tercets of terza rima
questions.explanation: A Shakespearean sonnet normally builds through three quatrains and can conclude with a pointed couplet.

questions.question: Gerard Manley Hopkins devised a compressed sonnet form of ten and a half lines. What is it called?
questions.explanation: The curtal sonnet contracts the proportions of the fourteen-line form to ten and a half lines.

questions.question: Which description best defines a traditional ballad?
options: A poem without any narrative action
A long poem primarily praising an object
A narrative song that tells a story
questions.explanation: Traditional ballads are narrative songs transmitted orally, often centred on dramatic events.

questions.question: Which rhyme scheme is especially common in the English ballad quatrain?
questions.explanation: The second and fourth lines of a traditional ballad quatrain usually rhyme: ABCB.

questions.question: A narrative poem uses repeated phrases, simple dialogue and short song-like stanzas. Which genre does this most strongly suggest?
questions.explanation: A plot-driven story with repetition and song-like stanzas is characteristic of a ballad.

questions.question: In the common English ballad metre, how do stresses typically alternate across four lines?
questions.explanation: Traditional ballad measure alternates four-stress and three-stress lines.

questions.question: A poem tells a compact supernatural story in quatrains with alternating four- and three-beat lines. Which classification is best supported?
options: An epic written in blank verse
A ballad using common ballad metre
questions.explanation: Storytelling and alternating four- and three-beat lines are hallmarks of the English ballad tradition.

questions.question: Which claim about literary ballads is the most accurate?
options: A ballad cannot contain a supernatural incident
Every ballad must have an unknown author
Named poets can adapt folk-ballad conventions in newly written works
All ballads must follow an identical rhyme scheme
questions.explanation: Literary ballads are authored poems that adapt techniques of orally transmitted folk ballads.

questions.question: A syllabus note confuses "ballad" with "ballade." Which distinction corrects it?
options: Both terms exclusively mean a fourteen-line poem
Ballad usually names a narrative song; ballade names a French fixed verse form
Ballad is necessarily unrhymed, while ballade is always an epic
Ballade is another name for blank verse
questions.explanation: The English ballad is a storytelling genre; the French ballade has prescribed stanzas and an envoy.

questions.question: Which central concern most commonly defines an elegy in English poetry?
options: A comic quarrel over a trivial object
The celebration of an athletic victory
questions.explanation: An elegy expresses mourning or reflective grief, often in response to death.

questions.question: Which poem is a pastoral elegy written by John Milton?
questions.explanation: Milton wrote Lycidas to mourn Edward King, using the shepherd-world conventions of pastoral elegy.

questions.question: An elegy’s emotional movement may end by offering which response to grief?
options: An unrelated invocation to a Muse
questions.explanation: Traditional elegies often move beyond lament toward consolation or a renewed perspective.

questions.question: What rhyme and metre define the English elegiac stanza associated with the eighteenth century?
questions.explanation: The English elegiac stanza is a four-line iambic-pentameter unit rhyming ABAB.

questions.question: Which pair consists of pastoral elegies mourning deceased poets or friends?
options: Keats’s Ode to a Nightingale and To Autumn
Byron’s Don Juan and Milton’s Paradise Lost
Pope’s The Rape of the Lock and Dryden’s Mac Flecknoe
questions.explanation: Lycidas and Adonais use pastoral conventions to memorialize Edward King and John Keats respectively.

questions.question: Which order best represents the conventional emotional progression of a traditional elegy?
options: A riddle, a quarrel, a witty final couplet
Lament, praise of the dead, consolation
questions.explanation: The elegiac movement commonly begins in grief, honours the lost person, and seeks consolation.

questions.question: Which statement avoids confusing a poetic genre with a metrical pattern?
options: All elegies must consist of fourteen lines
An elegy is identified chiefly by mournful subject matter, not by one compulsory rhyme scheme
Any poem written in quatrains is automatically an elegy
All elegies must use the ABAB elegiac stanza
questions.explanation: Elegy is a genre of mourning; the ABAB elegiac stanza is only one form elegies may use.

questions.question: An ode most typically addresses or celebrates what?
options: Only the death of a recently deceased poet
Only a petty event described satirically
A person, object, place or idea in an elevated lyric manner
questions.explanation: An ode is a formally sustained lyric of address, praise or contemplation.

questions.question: Which ancient Greek poet is associated with odes celebrating athletic victories?
questions.explanation: Pindaric odes grew out of Greek public praise poems celebrating athletic success.

questions.question: Which description better suits a Horatian ode than a Pindaric victory ode?
options: A fixed heroic plot told in twelve books
An obligatory celebration of Olympic champions
questions.explanation: Horatian odes are typically reflective and personal; Pindaric odes often celebrate public victories.

questions.question: Which work most clearly belongs to the ode tradition?
options: John Keats’s Ode on a Grecian Urn
Alexander Pope’s The Rape of the Lock
questions.explanation: Keats’s poem addresses an urn and uses it for sustained aesthetic reflection, a characteristic ode practice.

questions.question: A student says, "Every ode must have exactly fourteen lines." Which response is correct?
options: False because every ode must have eight lines instead
False; odes have varied stanza lengths and structures
True; all odes are therefore sonnets
questions.explanation: Ode describes a lyric mode of address and celebration; its stanza structures vary widely.

questions.question: A lyric directly addresses an abstract idea, moving from praise to reflective questioning. Which classification is strongest even without a fixed rhyme scheme?
questions.explanation: The sustained lyric address to an idea is characteristic of an ode, whose formal pattern may vary.

questions.question: Which comparison between ode and elegy is most defensible?
options: Odes typically address or contemplate a subject; elegies centrally explore loss and mourning
Odes must rhyme ABBA; elegies must be unrhymed
Both must have fourteen lines and a final couplet
Odes always narrate battles; elegies always mock trivial incidents
questions.explanation: Ode and elegy are distinguishable by their central literary purposes rather than a universally fixed line count.

questions.question: Which description most accurately defines an epic poem?
options: A long narrative of culturally or historically significant heroic action
A short comic refrain without narrative
A two-line lyric of private grief
questions.explanation: Epics sustain a heroic narrative on a large historical, mythic or cultural scale.

questions.question: Which work is an English epic by John Milton?
questions.explanation: Milton’s Paradise Lost is a major English epic dealing with the Fall of humankind.

questions.question: When a poet appeals to the Muse for inspiration at the opening of a heroic narrative, which epic convention is being used?
questions.explanation: An epic invocation directly addresses a Muse or deity for help in composing the poem.

questions.question: What is a canto in the structure of a long epic poem?
options: A mandatory refrain after each stanza
A substantial division comparable to a chapter
questions.explanation: Cantos are major subdivisions of epics and other long narrative poems.

questions.question: A lengthy comparison of a hero’s army to a natural phenomenon stretches across several lines. Which term fits this device?
questions.explanation: An epic simile is an extended comparison elaborated over multiple lines.

questions.question: Which statement about the verse form of English epics is correct?
options: All epics must be written in fourteen-line sonnets
An English epic can be written in unrhymed iambic pentameter, as Paradise Lost is
An epic cannot contain invocations or similes
An epic must always use rhyming heroic couplets
questions.explanation: Milton used unrhymed iambic pentameter in Paradise Lost, so epic is not limited to one rhyme pattern.

questions.question: What is the central technique of a mock epic?
options: Replacing all verse with plain historical records
Using grand epic conventions to treat a trivial or satiric subject
Composing only poems about the death of kings
questions.explanation: Mock epic gains satirical force by applying high epic style to relatively minor subjects.

questions.question: Who wrote the well-known mock epic The Rape of the Lock?
questions.explanation: Pope’s The Rape of the Lock transforms a social scandal into a mock-heroic conflict.

questions.question: Which work by John Dryden uses mock-epic technique to satirize a literary rival?
questions.explanation: Mac Flecknoe borrows elevated epic conventions to ridicule the poet Thomas Shadwell.

questions.question: A poet presents the loss of a fashionable accessory as a war of gods, champions and supernatural armies. Which genre is most appropriate?
questions.explanation: Treating a small social incident with grand epic machinery is the satirical disproportion of mock epic.

questions.question: What is the chief satirical effect when a mock-epic poet uses an invocation and heroic language for a minor quarrel?
options: The inflated style exposes the absurd disproportion between subject and treatment
The event is automatically made historically heroic
The story ceases to contain satire because epic devices are always sincere
The poem becomes a historical source about actual gods
questions.explanation: Mock epic contrasts grand narrative conventions with insignificant events to produce irony.
